name: Faropenem Sodium
meta: Schedule H1 – prescription only; pharmacist must keep a separate register
sections: White to light-yellow crystalline powder (sodium salt), freely soluble in water.

An oral penem (not a true carbapenem) marketed in Japan, India and Bangladesh. Concerns exist that its use may select cross-resistance to carbapenems, so stewardship guidance restricts its use. First approval/introduction: Japan 1997 (Suntory / Daiichi Asubio Pharma); India since mid-2000s; US FDA non-approvable (2006).

Binds penicillin-binding proteins, inhibiting bacterial cell-wall synthesis (bactericidal). Stable to most beta-lactamases including ESBLs; broad activity against Gram-positive, Gram-negative and anaerobic organisms. Receptor / target profile: Binds penicillin-binding proteins (high affinity for PBP2 and PBP1) inhibiting cell-wall synthesis; stable against many beta-lactamases including ESBLs and AmpC.
Summary: Bioavailability ~20–30%; Tmax ~1 h. ~90–95% protein bound. Half-life ~1 h. Excreted in urine (partly unchanged).
Upper and lower respiratory tract infections – pharyngitis, tonsillitis, sinusitis, acute bronchitis, community-acquired pneumonia
Uncomplicated and complicated urinary tract infections (including ESBL-producing organisms)
Gynaecological infections, otitis media, odontogenic infections
Adults: 150–300 mg three times daily (or 200 mg twice–three times daily) depending on severity
Use according to culture/sensitivity and stewardship policy
Dose to be individualised by the treating physician according to clinical response and tolerability.
Paediatric dosing per weight where approved.
Hypersensitivity to faropenem or other beta-lactams (history of anaphylaxis)
Reserve for infections where narrower agents are unsuitable (antimicrobial stewardship)
Sodium valproate – markedly reduced valproate levels (avoid)
Renal function; clinical response; C. difficile.
Clinical trials (largely Japan and India) show efficacy in respiratory, urinary and skin infections; stewardship bodies advise against routine use to preserve carbapenem activity.
Report severe diarrhoea, rash or breathing difficulty
Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from light and moisture. Keep out of the reach of children. Do not use after the expiry date.
